full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ. The vires of sub rules (3) and (4) of rule 4 of  উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিত করন ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, 1995 published by SRO No. 65-Ain/95/SM/ Bidhi-1/5-6/94 dated 2nd May, 1995 so far as it relates to counting the seniority from the date of regularization and in respect of cadre posts from the date of encadrement has been challenged by the respondents in the High Court Division, who were appointed in the development projects in The Bangladesh Agriculture Resource Institute under the Ministry of Agriculture. The High Court Division made the rule absolute declaring the notification dated 12th March, 2003, to be ultra the constitution. 

 3. With petitioner No. 1 after obtaining the postgraduate degree in soil, science from the University of Dhaka entered into the service of the soil Resources Development Institute on 5th May, 1986 as scientific officer and the writ petitioner Nos. 2-4 after obtaining Bachelor's Degree in Agriculture joined the service as scientific officers with similar scales. Thereafter the writ petitioner Nos. 3 and 4 obtained, the post graduation degrees in soil science. They were initially appointed in a development project with a clear assurance that on completion of the initial project period they would be included and absorbed in the revenue set up. In due course they were included in the revenue set up on 5th June, 1993, The writ respondent Nos. 6-17 were originally appointed under the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute (BARI) in the Analytical Service Division as scientific officers with the identical scales. They were junior to the writ petitioners and were doing the same nature of job and thy had entered into the service of the autonomous institute of the BARI long after the writ petitioners entry in the service. But writ respondent Nos. 11-17 entered in the service of the BARI after the writ petitioners were included in the revenue set up the government. Thus the writ petitioners are senior in service at the entry point as scientific officers and also in the revenue set up. The writ respondent Nos.6-17 were included in the government service on 20th May 1993 and they had joined the government service with effect from 1st October, 1993. The writ petitioners were brought under the project effective from 1st July, 1992 and the writ respondent Nos. 6-12 were brought into government service effective from 1st January, 1993, By circular No.7053/1/Civ-11 dated 3rd March, 1985, the government promulgated the Recruitment Rules for those who were appointed in development projects prior to the transfer of the officers and staff from the development projects prior to the transfer of the officers and staff from the development project to revenue budge. Subsequently the Ministry of Establishment now public Administration had issued circular dated 11th January, 1992 specifically providing a time frame of not exceeding six months for regularization of the service of the persons brought into revenue set up from the Development projects. 

 4. In the case of Gazetted officers their regularization required consultation with the PSC and it was made obligatory to finalize as per recruitment Rules and sent requisition to the PSC for regularization. The PSC was also required by the afore-said circular to complete all formalities for regularization within a minimum period of five months. The Ministry of Agriculture sat over the matter of regularization of the service of the writ petitioners till 10th May, 1999, on which date, they were regularized. The writ respondent Nos. 6-17 who entered in the government service from the autonomous body of BARI were neither regularized, nor their appointment in class-1 government posts were approved by the president though their services were confirmed by the competent authority. Thus the writ respondent Nos. 6-17 though doing the same job as scientific officer junior in service to the writ petitioners, the Ministry of Agriculture issued a notification under SRO No. 10/Law/2003 dated 12th January, 2003, purporting to be an amendment to the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute ordinance, 1976 (Ordinance No. XXII of 1976) providing that the officers who were transferred from BARI to government service had been granted seniority from the date of their original appointment in the BARI. It was a colorable legislation which is in conflict with articles 27 and 29 (1) of the constitution and the provisions of the services (Re-organization and conditions) Act, 1975 and the Amendment to the soil Resources Development Institute (Officers and staff) service Regulations, 1998. 

 5. Admittedly, the writ petitioners were appointed on a development project on different dates. Some of them were appointed in 1986, some of them were appointed later on but they did not give the exact date in their appointments. Their services were regularized by a notification under memo dated 5th June, 1993, with effect from 1st July, 1992 on temporary basis for a period of six months and then they were permanently absorbed in the revenue set up by notification dated 10th May, 1999, on the recommendation of the public service commission. It has been mentioned therein that their seniority will be decided in accordance with rule 3 of Rules of 1995. Their claim is that writ respondent Nos. 6-17 entered in the service on 1st October, 1993, and therefore, they are junior to them. They claimed that the Ministry of public Administration in violation of the Rules regularized their service in the revenue set up much latter than they were legally entitled to be absorbed. 

 6. The High court was of the view that the service of the writ petitioners were regularized with effect from 10th May, 1999, although as per public Administration's circular under memo dated 11th January, 1992, their regularization should have been made within six months from the date of their absorption on temporary basis on 1st July, 1992,. It further observed that they had acquired a right of regularization within six months from the date of ad-hoc appointment but for the neglect or lathes on the part of the government, they were made junior to some of the writ respondents, and therefore, the notification dated 12th January, 2003 ultra vires articles 27 and 29 (1) of the constitution. By this notification the president in exercise of powers under article 142 of the constitution amended rule 6 of Soil Resources Development Institute officers and Employees Appointment Rules, 1998. The amendment is reproduced below: 

 7. The Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institutes employees and officers having been transferred to the soil Resources Development Institute, those employees and officers would be deemed to have been appointed from the date of joining in the government service and that they will get seniority, pension benefits etc. from , the date of joining. 

 8. It is on record that there was no law or rules or regulations prescribing the procedure to be followed for regularization of the officers and employees appointed in development projects in the revenue set up. It is only by SRO 65 under memo dated 2nd May, 1995, the government formulated the Rules. The procedure to be following for regularization has been mentioned in rule 3 thereon. This rule provides inter alia that- 

 a) in a revenue budget post if an officer or employee is appointed on temporary basis in a project and if his appointment is made after following the appointment procedures of the government, the service of such officer or employee will be regularised. 

 d) if an officer or employee of the revenue budget is on leave preparatory retirement or is retired from the service, his service be treated with retrospective effect from the date of leave preparatory retirement or the retirement, as the case may be, but his service must be satisfactory till the date of leave preparatory retirement. 

 (a) the seniority will be counted from the date of regularization of an officer or employee but if an officer or employee is appointed whose service has been regularised after regularization   of an officer or employee" appointed later on due to shortage of relevant service record, who has been working in the same project, the officer or employee who has been appointed earlier will get seniority. 

 (b) in case of appointment of an officer or employee appointed on the same day, the seniority will be decided in the following manner: 

 (c) if the date of appointment in the project of an officer or employee is the same with an officer or employee of the revenue budget, the officer or employee appointed in the revenue budget shall gel seniority. 

 (d) if an officer or employee is encadered by the public service com-mission later on, their seniority will be decided from the date of encadrement. 

 10. On consideration of almost similar Rules in, respect of officers and employees of development projects, who have been regularised in the revenue set up, this court in LGED v. Mizanur Rahman 17 BLC (AD) 91, held as under: 

 (i) Whenever any vacancy in LGED is created in the revenue set up, it shall consider for absorption of employees or officers of the development projects within the meaning of section 2 (ga) of the Rule, 2005, If the project in which s/he is working is completed subject to the condition that such employee or officer has requisite qualifications for the said post. 

 (ii) whenever a vacant post is created in the revenue budget, the WED shall absorb/transfer an employee or officer from the development project mentioned in clause (1) to fill up that post in accordance with Rules of 1985 and the ECNEC's decision dated 10th January, 2008. 

 (iii) An officer or employee shall be absorbed if s/he was appointed in the development project within the meaning or rule 2 (ka) of Rules, 2005 in accordance with the procedures prescribed for appointment in public employment. 

 (iv) An officer or employee must have requisite qualifications for the post in which he is seeking absorption. 

 (v) An officer or employee must have continuity in service in the project in which he is working. 

 (vi) An officer or employee must have satisfactory service record before his case is considered for regularization in the revenue budget. 

 (vii) If an officer and employee whose rank and status does not relate to the posts advertised by the impugned notifications on the day of its publications, such officer or employee would not be eligible for consideration for absorption. 

 (viii) The employees and officers who have been working in the development projects mentioned in clause (1) on monthly pay basis would only be eligible for consideration for absorption in the revenue budget. 

 (ix) Unless and until vacancies in the revenue budget in the LGED are created, the employees and officers of the development project mentioned in clause (1) cannot claim as of right to be absorbed in the revenue budget; 

 (x) While considering and selecting an employee or officer of the development project for absorption in the revenue budget, the appointing authority shall maintain strictly the prevailing quota system for employment in the public employment being following by the Government. 

 (xi) The LGED shall consider the cases of those working on master roll basis for absorption in the revenue budget by phases if they have requisite qualifications subject to availability of vacancies according to their seniority. 

 12. Now taking these Rules as it stand, whether the writ petitioners can claim seniority over the write respondents. Admittedly the writ petitioners have been transferred in the revenue budget temporarily on 1st July, 1992, on which date, three was no rules regulating their seniority. They could claim seniority. They could claim seniority in pursuance of rule 4 of the Rules circulated by SRO NO. 65 dated 2nd May, 1995. There is no denial of the fact that they had been regularized by order dated 9th November, 2003 with retrospective from 10th May, 1999 as per Rules of 1995. They have accepted their regularization and did not take any exception because of rule 4 of Rules of 1995. The writ respondents have been appointed on regular basis. They were not appointed on any project, and therefore, the writ petitioners cannot claim seniority over the regular employee. It is true that as per Ministry of public Administration's Circular under memo dated 11th January, 1998, there was a direction for regularization within six months from the date of creation of post in the revenue set up but the authority did not act as per direction. This circular may be taken as pious desire of the authority and directory in nature. It has no force of law. More so, this circular will not prevail over. Rules of 1995, which have force of law within meaning of article 152 of the constitution. 

 13. Under rule 4 of Rules 1995, the criteria for determining the seniority has been spelt out. In presence of these Rules, the writ petitioners cannot claim any right on the basis of the circular of the Ministry of জনপ্রশাসান, dated 11th January, 1992. The High court Division without declaring the rule 4 of the regularization and Determination of Seniority of the employee transferred from the development projects declared the writ petitioners as senior to the writ respondents mainly on the reasoning that had they been regularized within six months they would not have opposed rule 4. How fallacy the opinion is? A rule which has force of law cannot be ignored or impeded its enforceability only because it is in conflict with the circular. It failed to notice that the circular which has been circulated by a Ministry which has no force of law. It is issued for the purpose of internal departmental officials to follow the guidelines and the violation of any of the provision does not confer a right upon an officer or employee, which can be enforceable by law. Secondly, the Rules have been promulgated by the government in accordance with the provisions of the constitution, which will prevail upon the circular. 

 14. Rule 6 ka in the soil Resources Development institute (officers and staff) Recruitment Rules, 1998 has been added by the president in exercise of powers under article 140 (2) of the constitution in prior consultation with PSC providing that by reason of transfer of the officers and employees of Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute to soil Resources Development Institute, their services shall be deemed to be employee of the latter institute from the date of joining in the service and that their benefits and seniority will be determined accordingly. The substance of the amendment of the Rules by means of addition of a rule is that the officers and employee who have been appointed in Bangladesh Agricultural Research institute shall get their seniority with retrospective effect from the date of joining in the service by reason of their transfer to the Soil Resources Development Institute. 

 16. Craies on Statute Law, Seventh Edn. it is said, 'Every law that takes away or impairs rights vested agreeably to existing is retrospective, and is generally unjust and may be oppressive' it is a good general rule that a law should have no retrospect, but in cases in which the laws may justly and for the benefit of the community and also of individuals relate to a time antecedent to their commencement; as statutes of oblivion or of pardon. They are certainly retrospective, and literally both concerning and after the facts committed.' As a general rule of law that statutes are not to operate retrospectively but sometimes it is expressly enacted that an enactment shall be retrospective. Craies in the same edition at page 392 said that if it is a necessary implication from the language employed that the legislature intended a particular section to have a retrospective operation, the courts will give it such an operation. 

 17. In the chapter of 'Statutes virtually retrospective' craies at page 396 said, sometimes a statute, although not intended to be retrospective, will in fact have a retrospective operation. For instance, if two persons enter into a contract, and afterwards a statute is passed, which, as Cockburn, C.J. said in Duke of Devonshire V. Barrow (1877) 2QBD 286 'engrafts an enactment Rayon existing contracts' and thus operates so as to produce a result which is something   quite different from the original intention of the contracting parties, such a statute has, in effect, a retrospective operation.' As observed above, the writ petitioners existing rights under the Rules  have not been taken away. More so, the language used in the amendment has no ambiguity and in clear terms it is said that it will have retrospective operation under such situation the court cannot give it prospective operative. 

 18. The views expressed by of the High Court Division that the writ petitioners' were appointed in the development project and ultimately they were included in the revenue set up in 1983 with effect from 01.07.1992 and it was duty of the government to make them regularized and having not done so, obviously made the writ petitioners junior are not inconformity with law. It must assign reason why the amendment of the Rules should not be given retrospective operation. This court in Bangladesh Rtd. Govt. Employees welfare Association v. Bangladesh, 51 DLR (AD) 121 observed that a legislative enactment or a government action cannot be knocked down as unconstitutional even if it results in equality or is even shocking to the conscience unless such enactment or such action is violative of any provision of the constitution or law and that inequity or unconscionable effect cannot be rectified by the court applying article 27. If a diffential treatment satisfies the twin test of logical classification and reasonableness, it cannot be shocking to conscience. There will always be difference between a man and another man or a pensioner and another pensioner, but the question is whether such difference has any relevance in search of nexus between the object of the legislation and the classification made observed in Air-way Electric Appliance Corp. V. Day (1924) 266 US 71. 

 20. Assuming that rule 4 is inconsistent with article 27 and 29 (1) of the constitution, the High Court Division did not declare it as such. It has declared the notification dated 12th January, 2003 of the Ministry of Agriculture without making any observation as to whether this notification ultra vires rule 4 of Rules 1995. What is surprising to note here is that neither the writ petitioners made sufficient pleadings in support of their claim that rule 6ka of Soil Resources Development Institute Recruitment Rules, 1998 ultra vires rule 4 of the Rules of 1985, they made any statement nor did the High Court Division make any findings or observations in this regard and abruptly declared rule 6 ultra vires articles 27 and 29 (1). 

 21. We would, however, like to observe here that we have been noticing in good number of cases that despite there are provisions for regularization of the service of employees or officers in the revenue set up either within six months or within such time as soon as the posts in the revenue budget are lying vacant, the government or the PSC intentionally delays in the process of regularizing their service and sometimes, it recommends some junior employees or officers to the PSC for regularization and then recommend the senior employees to the PSC for regularization, who have been appointed on ad-hoc basis earlier with the result that the junior employees or officers get seniority and status over the senior employees and officers. This has created anomaly in the service of different departments. This discriminatory treatment should be avoided. Henceforth, it is directed that if any post in the revenue budget lies vacant, the employee or officer who is eligible for appointment to the said post should be regularized and if such appointment requires recommendation of the PSC his name should be recommended in due time so that he should not be deprived of his right of seniority than the junior employee of officer.
